question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}(x+2y), & 1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{17}{30},$ find $\text{E}[X+2Y].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $1\le x\le 2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{2}{5}(x+2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{[xy+{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}(x+1-0) \\  & =\frac{2(x+1)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot \frac{2(x+1)}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{\int }_{1}^{2}({x}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}(\frac{8}{3}+2-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{23}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X+2Y] & =\text{E}[X]+2\text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{23}{15}+2(\frac{17}{30}) \\  & =\frac{23}{15}+\frac{17}{15} \\  & =\frac{40}{15} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
